clue.text: Information on position for patient?

parts.note: reads as a hospital chart about how a sick person is lying, but the patient is the biblical sufferer of that name and the position a post at work

explanation.definitionFit: A written outline of what a post involves is information about that position; the patient man of the Bible lends his name to its first word.

clue.text: Job cuts due here could produce a tragic tale

indicators.note: the letters of the four words before it could be made into something new, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Redundancies announced at a workplace could make for a sad story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could produce' rearranges JOBCUTSDUEHERE. The answer is Thomas Hardy's bleak novel of 1895.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardy's novel about the doomed stonemason Jude Fawley is a famously tragic story.

clue.text: Where one waits to be transported with kiss first

definitions.text: Where one waits to be transported

parts.note: buss is an old word for a kiss
top means first, as in top of the class

explanation.surface: Someone waits to be carried away, but wants a kiss before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside stop is the spot where passengers wait to be carried away by a public vehicle.

clue.text: Reconstructed by one furniture-maker

indicators.note: something reconstructed has been rebuilt in a new form, so these letters are put together differently

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture has been rebuilt by a single craftsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reconstructed' rearranges BYONE. The definition is cheeky: the dark hardwood is a material furniture is made from, not a carpenter.
explanation.definitionFit: This dense black hardwood has long been used to make fine cabinets and other furniture.

clue.text: Keen to plug old opening in city

indicators.note: a plug fills a hole, so the pieces before these words are stuffed into the middle of the next one

parts.note: to keen is to wail in grief, to cry
a vent is an opening that lets air or smoke out

explanation.surface: An eager person wants to block an ancient gateway in a town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like eager, but here it is the verb meaning to wail in mourning. Coventry is a city in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Coventry is a cathedral city in the English West Midlands.

clue.text: Fashionable reference book cut charge

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing

indicators.note: the reference book is shortened, keeping only its first four letters

parts.note: a dictionary is a reference book

explanation.surface: A trendy reference book has been abridged and now faces a charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims DICTIONARY to DICT, its usual abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To indict someone is to formally accuse them of a crime, so the verb works as charge.

clue.text: International meeting to see if strike is possible?

definitions.meaning: a game of cricket between two national sides

definitions.text: to see if strike is possible?
definitions.meaning: a trial of a single wooden stick to find out whether it will light

explanation.definitionFit: A cricket fixture between countries is one sense; trying one stick from a box to check it ignites is the other.

clue.text: Get a male to reform, essential when doing porridge

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it, so the letters of the three words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting a man to mend his ways is vital while he is serving time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges AMALETO, taking in 'to' as well as 'a male'. 'Doing porridge' is British slang for serving a prison sentence, but here it means making the breakfast dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground oats are the basic ingredient needed when cooking the hot breakfast dish.

clue.text: Anti-tax demonstration by apparently brave group

definitions.text: Anti-tax demonstration by apparently brave group

parts.words: Anti-tax demonstration by apparently brave group
parts.note: a 1773 protest against a duty on a drink, carried out by colonists disguised as Native American warriors, called braves

explanation.definitionFit: Colonists dressed as Mohawk braves dumped taxed cargo into a Massachusetts harbour, a famous protest against British duties.

clue.text: Ended as last letter in' crossword is worked out

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word that follows is taken

parts.note: a puzzle worked out has been solved

explanation.surface: The crossword was finished when its last letter went in.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures filling in the final square of a grid; the last letter of 'crossword' is D, which starts the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A partnership or marriage that is dissolved has been formally brought to an end.

clue.text: Determined to fight

parts.note: set means determined, as in set on winning

explanation.surface: Someone is resolved to have a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Determined to' looks like one phrase about resolve; split it after the first word, leaving the noun at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a brief, heated quarrel or scuffle.

clue.text: Inferior way to keep dry in river -

indicators.note: one piece is told to keep another, so the second goes inside the first

parts.note: the Tay is the longest river in Scotland
TT, teetotal, means dry, abstaining from alcohol

explanation.surface: A poor method for staying dry while out on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inferior way' reads as one phrase, but only 'Inferior' defines. TT stands for teetotal, a crossword convention for dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shabby and worn is of poor quality, second-rate.

clue.text: Communist leaders in Number Ten, perhaps? My lips are sealed!

indicators.note: the leaders of the political word are placed inside the other pieces
perhaps hints that the three letters of the word before can be rearranged
only the leading part of the political word is kept, its first four letters

explanation.surface: Asked whether Communists head the government at Downing Street, a spokesman declines to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: Number Ten is the British Prime Minister's Downing Street residence, which sets up the political picture; 'perhaps' rearranges TEN to ENT, and 'leaders' keeps COMM from Communist.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying nothing on a matter is the stock refusal a spokesperson gives, the same as declaring one's lips sealed.

clue.text: International exhibition's confident outlook

parts.note: an expo is a large international trade or world fair
sure means confident, certain

explanation.surface: A world fair displays an optimistic view of the future.
explanation.definitionFit: A building's exposure is the direction it faces and the view it commands, its outlook.

clue.text: On selected occasions, quite a paper!

parts.note: some means quite a, as in that's some newspaper
The Times is a British newspaper

explanation.surface: An admiring exclamation about what a remarkable newspaper this is.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface praises the very paper the puzzle appeared in.
explanation.definitionFit: Now and then, at certain moments but not always, is what the adverb conveys.

clue.text: As last resort, elected dictator

indicators.note: to resort is to sort again, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

parts.note: a candidate elected is in

explanation.surface: Turning to dictatorship as a final option, a tyrant is chosen at the polls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As last resort' reads as one idiom; 'resort' is re-sort, rearranging LAST to STAL, then IN for elected.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Stalin was the autocratic ruler of the Soviet Union from the 1920s to 1953.

clue.text: Piece of music' put back in programme — open otherwise

indicators.note: put back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A piece of music is restored to a concert programme that would otherwise have been left open.
explanation.walkthrough: MEOPENOT sits in 'programme — open otherwise' and 'put back' turns it round. A tone poem is an orchestral work telling a story, like those by Richard Strauss.
explanation.definitionFit: A symphonic poem is a single-movement orchestral composition that illustrates a story or scene.

clue.text: Sweeps get black — dreadful mess, nothing covered

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: the zero is covered over by the scrambled letters around it
dreadful hints that the letters of the next word are in a bad state, rearranged

parts.note: O, the round figure, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Chimney sweeps come out blackened and in an awful mess, with nothing left clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' rearranges MESS to ESMS, and 'covered' puts O inside that, after B.
explanation.definitionFit: Besoms are brooms made of twigs bound to a handle, things that sweep.

clue.text: Fine collection put on exhibition :

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece is placed on top of the second

parts.note: a set is a collection of things
a fair is an exhibition, as in a trade fair

explanation.surface: A fine set of items has been placed on show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' is the weather sense: a barometer marked set fair promises settled sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: Set fair describes weather that is settled and sunny, so it means fine.

clue.text: Friendliness one found in good French environment

parts.note: bon is French for good

indicators.note: one piece is found inside another, so the numeral goes into the middle of the word for surroundings

parts.note: home is one's environment, the place one lives
I, the Roman numeral, stands for one

explanation.surface: A friendly person discovered in pleasant French surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonhomie is cheerful good nature, a warm friendliness.

clue.text: Democrat in. European house becomes President

indicators.note: the party member is placed inside the foreign word for a dwelling

parts.note: maison is French for house

explanation.surface: A Democrat moves into a house in Europe and rises to become President.
explanation.walkthrough: D goes in MAISON. James Madison was the fourth US President.
explanation.definitionFit: James Madison served as the fourth head of state of the United States.

clue.text: Fish one found lying on bed

definitions.meaning: a smoked herring, split and cured
someone having a kip, a sleeper

explanation.definitionFit: A smoked herring is one sense; the other is a person taking a kip, a nap, on a bed.

clue.text: Allow little time to cook fettucini

indicators.note: cooking changes food, so the letters of the pasta's name are mixed up into something new

explanation.surface: Leave yourself only a few minutes to prepare a dish of pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave only a narrow margin of time is to cut it fine.

clue.text: Are customers of penthouse restaurant so disgruntled?

definitions.text: Are customers of penthouse restaurant so disgruntled?

parts.words: Are customers of penthouse restaurant so disgruntled?
parts.note: diners at a rooftop eatery are served their meals high in the building

explanation.definitionFit: Diners eating high up are literally served up top, and the idiom means bored and annoyed.

clue.text: Physical nature of spire, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a fleche is a slender spire, often over the crossing of a church

explanation.surface: Something about the bodily character of a church tower.
explanation.walkthrough: FLECHE, a thin spire, is said like the answer. The apostrophe-free spelling of the French word is used.
explanation.definitionFit: The body as opposed to the spirit, our corporeal side, is called the flesh.

clue.text: Prepare once more to fight behind militant leader

parts.note: rear means behind, at the back

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Getting ready to fight again, standing behind a hardline leader.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearm is to equip with weapons again, getting ready for renewed war.

clue.text: Academic supporting ordinary soldiers

parts.note: to profess a cause or faith is to declare open support for it
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers, not officers

explanation.surface: A university teacher is backing the rank and file of the army.
explanation.walkthrough: The equivalence is loose: to profess a creed is to declare allegiance to it, so supporting stands for PROFESS. OR is the services abbreviation for other ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior university teacher holding a chair is the archetypal academic.

clue.text: Gentleman booked after dreadful stir, taking drink on public transport

indicators.note: in an across entry, the drink on the transport comes after it
dreadful says the letters of the next word are in a terrible state, rearranged

parts.note: a tram is a form of public transport
a shandy is beer mixed with lemonade

explanation.surface: A man, having made an awful fuss, gets a drink while riding a bus or tram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' rearranges STIR to TRIS. Sterne's novel is The Life and Opinions of Tristram Shandy, Gentleman, so he is a gentleman in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterne's comic novel names its narrator as a gentleman in its full title, so he is literally a gentleman put in a book.
